criteria.note: GENERIC, by-reference config. resolve_bootstrap_config reads every input from config['bootstrap'] (project_key; required_project_type default company-managed; issue_types default Epic/Task; statuses default the nine-status lifecycle {name, category}) alongside the existing routing/status_map/trackers; base_url + token_ref (a SECRET REFERENCE, never a raw credential) are read by build_live_provisioner from the jira-cloud connection block. A malformed block fails closed by name (BootstrapError) at resolve time (blank project_key, empty issue_types, empty/bad-category statuses, duplicate status name each raise). The AC1 grep (bcengi/dejitech/.atlassian.net) is CLEAN in tracker_jira_init.py and tracker_adapter.py. The second-adopter property holds: no company- or board-specific CONFIG literal - an adopter drops in their own bootstrap block. See note-1 on the 'Veldo' brand word in three docstring lines (prose, not config).

DETECT-FIRST, FAIL-LOUD, no half-board. provision_board calls provisioner.project_type(project) as its FIRST act and raises BootstrapError before any provision_issue_type/provision_status when actual != required; the message names the project (PROJ), its actual type (team-managed), the required type (company-managed), and the remediation (recreate as company-managed and re-run). Reproduced independently: a real team-managed board is refused with zero statuses provisioned (no half-board). TOOTH reproduced: neutralizing 'if actual != required:' to 'if False and ...' in an in-memory copy provisions all nine statuses on a team-managed board while the on-disk module refuses; tracker_jira_init.py sha256 unchanged.

IDEMPOTENT statuses + workflow. provision_status is create-or-reuse BY NAME (created=False on reuse); wire_status_into_workflow is wire-if-absent (False when already reachable); both added to the TrackerAdapter base seam (audited only on an actual write) and modeled by the FakeTracker. Reproduced independently: a fresh company-managed board -> created 9, wired 18 (9 statuses x both issue types); a re-run -> created 0, wired 0, reused 9, already_wired 18, state_digest byte-identical; a partial board (Backlog, Ready seeded) -> created 7, reused 2, all nine present after (absent status created, not skipped). TOOTH reproduced: neutralizing the FakeTracker create-or-reuse guard makes a re-run DUPLICATE (created 9) while the real path stays created 0; tracker_adapter.py sha256 unchanged. Reads are side-effect-free (write audit unchanged after project_type/existing_status_names/workflow_status_names/existing_issue_types).

REUSES the shipped mirror, reinvents nothing. bootstrap() calls tracker_mirror_runner.run_from_repo over the SAME provisioner object after provision_board, feeding tracker_mirror.mirror_events / mirror_plan_events (WARP-0605/0606/1004..1006); tracker_jira_init.py adds no projection rule of its own (grep confirms no epic/child projection logic in the module - it delegates). Reproduced via selfcheck fixture: bootstrap over a fixture spec/plan index + event stream provisions the board (created 9) AND creates one epic + >=1 child; a second pass leaves the epic count at 1 and state_digest byte-identical (the mirror's marker-keyed upsert forks nothing).

ONE command, guarded, reference-wired live edge. bin/warp routes 'jira' to the repo-only .warp/tracker_jira_init.py behind the same existence guard as 'warp mirror' (a pack that did not lay the module fails loud and honestly, not an import error). warp jira init --dry-run previews the whole bootstrap over a FakeTracker seeded as the required type with NO issue types and NO statuses and the instance catalog stocked, so it shows what would be added, with no network and no token; without --dry-run build_live_provisioner constructs the reference JiraCompanyManagedProvisioner (a JiraCloudAdapter subclass). Reproduced independently: build_live_provisioner FAILS CLOSED by name when no token resolves ('no token resolved from env:...') and when no jira-cloud tracker is configured. No timer/daemon/auto-start; nothing detached (NG1). bin/warp is byte-identical across root + plugin/templates + 6 packs (sha256 d47cbe12...).

Selftest drives the WHOLE bootstrap over the deterministic FakeTracker offline and is NON-TAUTOLOGICAL. Independently reran scripts/selftest.py: 2346 passed, 0 failed. The assertions track the real gap (created 9 on empty, 7 on partial; issue types 1 added on a project missing Epic, 0 on a full one). All in-memory source-mutation teeth reproduced from scratch and each turned RED while the on-disk modules stayed byte-unchanged (see AC2/AC3/AC7 notes). None of the four teeth is vacuous.

The founder-directed core HOLDS: ensure types exist, add missing, NEVER a wrong type, run FIRST. A vendor-neutral issue-type seam (existing_issue_types read-only; provision_issue_type ensure-present, idempotent by name, audited only on an actual attach) was added to the TrackerAdapter base and modeled by the FakeTracker (per-project issue-type set + an instance catalog of addable types). provision_board ensures EVERY configured type AFTER the team-managed fail-loud and BEFORE statuses/wiring/mirror - reproduced independently: the write audit order is provision_issue_type, provision_issue_type, provision_status, wire_status_into_workflow (issue types strictly before status + wire). A project missing Epic (has only Task, instance holds Epic) -> issue_types_created 1, Epic present after; a re-run adds nothing; a project holding both is a no-op. A configured type absent from the INSTANCE fails loud by name (TrackerItemNotFound naming Epic) with NO wrong-type fallback (_provision_issue_type raises when match is None; it never selects a different type - a plan is never mapped onto a Sub-task). TWO TEETH reproduced: (A) neutralizing the FakeTracker add-missing write ('types.add(name)' removed) leaves Epic ABSENT while the real fake adds it; (B) neutralizing the never-in-instance guard ('if False and name not in self._instance_issue_types') INVENTS a type the instance does not hold while the real fake refuses by name. tracker_adapter.py sha256 unchanged after both. The live JiraCompanyManagedProvisioner endpoints (GET /rest/api/3/issuetype, GET /rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/project + /issuetypescheme/mapping, POST /rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/{schemeId}/issuetype) are plausible per Jira Cloud REST v3, reference-wired, and never run in the gate.

findings.text: note-1 (non-blocking, cosmetic). The word 'Veldo' appears in three lines of tracker_jira_init.py (module docstring lines 2 and 7, and the main() ArgumentParser description on line 651) as the framework/board brand word ('the live Veldo board'). It is descriptive PROSE, not a config value: no adopter input flows through it, all inputs are read by reference, and the second-adopter property is unaffected. It is worth flagging only because (a) no sibling .warp module and no other spec uses 'Veldo' - every released module says WARP or 'the board', so this is a naming drift local to WARP-0612, and (b) the VELDO rename/OSS decision was PARKED with the repo name staying WARP. Recommend a follow-up prose swap to 'WARP board' / 'the board' for house-style consistency. Does not affect shipped behavior; the spec's own AC1 grep (bcengi/dejitech/atlassian host) is clean.

note-2 (non-blocking, process). The builder committed proof/WARP-0612/manifest.json INTO the impl commits: the manifest is git-tracked and the version inside d023021 binds to the PARENT d561bfd. The correct pattern (sibling WARP-1212) keeps proof untracked until the evidence commit, so the manifest binds to the commit it proves. The orchestrator has already REBOUND the working-tree manifest to d023021, where it validates (validate.py proof exit 0) and its proof_digest is stable (sha256:b1f545bc5d385b01).
